title: Language Structures and Editing
summary: Phrases and clauses, relative clauses, conditionals, modals, participles and dangling modifiers, punctuation for effect, and editing for concord, tense and ambiguity.

items: A **phrase** has no finite verb: 'after the storm', 'running late'.
A **clause** has a subject and a finite verb. A **main clause** can stand alone; a **subordinate clause** cannot: 'because the road was closed'.
**Relative clauses** begin with who, whom, whose, which or that. A **non-defining** clause adds extra information and is set off by commas: 'My brother, who lives in Polokwane, is a nurse.'

rows: If you heat ice, it melts.
If it rains, we will cancel the match.
If I won the lottery, I would travel.
If I had studied, I would have passed.

notes.text: Modal verbs express degrees of certainty, obligation or permission: **must** (obligation or strong certainty), **should** (advice), **may/might** (possibility), **can/could** (ability or permission), **will/would** (future or willingness).

notes.title: Fixing a dangling modifier
notes.problem: 'Walking to school, the rain soaked my blazer.'
steps: The opening phrase 'Walking to school' must describe the subject.
As written, it says the rain was walking.
notes.answer: 'While I was walking to school, the rain soaked my blazer.'

notes.text: **Ambiguity** occurs when a sentence has two possible meanings: 'The police shot the man with a gun.' (Did the man have the gun?) Rewrite to make the meaning clear.

notes.label: Punctuation for effect
notes.text: **Dash**: adds emphasis or an afterthought. **Ellipsis (…)**: omission, a trailing thought or suspense. **Exclamation mark**: strong emotion. **Inverted commas** around a single word can suggest sarcasm: 'Our "reliable" train was late again.'

'After the long holiday' is a clause.

questions.memo: ✓✓ e.g. 'Having finished the exam, I heard the bell ring.' / 'After I had finished the exam, the bell rang.' (2)

questions.prompt: Combine using a non-defining relative clause: 'Ms Dlamini teaches Grade 11. She won a national award.'
questions.memo:
✓ Ms Dlamini, who teaches Grade 11, (1)
✓ won a national award. (commas correct) (1)

questions.prompt: Explain the ambiguity and rewrite: 'I saw the girl with the binoculars.'
questions.memo:
✓ It is unclear whether I used binoculars or the girl had them (1)
✓ e.g. 'Using binoculars, I saw the girl.' (1)
